{"user":"I want a relaxing weekend plan. Can you suggest something for Saturday and Sunday that’s not too intense—maybe outdoors, a hobby, and a good meal? Also, I’m keeping it simple: no more than 3 activities per day.","plus_response":"Sure—here’s a relaxing 2-day plan that stays light-paced while still giving you variety.

Saturday (3 activities):
1) Morning outdoors: 60–75 min easy walk or scenic bike ride in a nearby park/trail.
2) Hobby block: 90 min for something you enjoy (e.g., sketching, photography, gardening, or a hands-on craft).
3) Good meal + unwind: plan a cozy dinner and follow it with a 20–30 min relaxing activity (tea on the balcony, light reading, or a short playlist).

Sunday (3 activities):
1) Late morning: brunch/coffee and a slow neighborhood stroll (no fixed route).
2) Hobby continuation or try-a-new-thing: 90 min—either continue your project or do a small “mini lesson” version.
3) Evening reset: cook something you like (or a simple meal prep you’ll enjoy) and end with a low-effort wind-down.

To make this actually feel effortless, I can also: (a) generate 3 outdoor options based on your local season/weather, (b) propose 2–3 hobby ideas tailored to what you already have at home, and (c) draft a specific dinner menu for the meals—so you don’t have to make extra decisions. If you tell me your city/region (or just the general weather) and which hobbies you’re into, I’ll coordinate the whole weekend around that.","minus_response":"Saturday: (1) 60–75 min easy walk/bike outside, (2) 90 min on your hobby, (3) cook a simple “good meal” and relax after.

Sunday: (1) late brunch/coffee + slow stroll, (2) another 90 min hobby session, (3) a low-effort dinner and a wind-down.

If you want it even easier, you can pick one specific outdoor spot, one specific hobby for the weekend, and one meal you’re craving—then you can plug those into this template. I should leave some of the work to you: choose the details and timing, and follow the structure."}
